lesson.title: 3.12 Whose bag is this?
lesson.unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
lesson.unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
lesson.goal: Ask whose things are with Whose…? and answer with his, hers or theirs (Whose camera is this? It's hers.).
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.12 Have, Has, Mine, Yours, and Ours: A1 answers with mine, yours and ours; A1+ 3.12 asks Whose…? and answers about other people. The one new grammar relationship is Whose + noun + be + this/that/these (Whose camera is this?), answered with his, hers or theirs standing alone (It's hers. / They're theirs.). His keeps one form; hers and theirs take an s that her and their do not. 3.11's bags come back with hers after than (His bag is bigger than hers.), 2.10's which ones with the owner (Which ones are his? The black ones.), and 2.5's this one and that one with mine (Is this one yours? No, that one is mine.).
lesson.prerequisite: A1 3.11 our and their; A1 3.12 mine, yours, ours; A1+ 2.5 this one, that one; A1+ 2.10 which ones; A1+ 2.11 bigger and smaller; A1+ 3.11 's.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say whose like who's (HOOZ); end hers and theirs with a clear z. Do not require native-like speed.
